author: codereport
body:
I have been meaning to open this PR for a while. While writing my ARRAY 2022 paper [Combinators and Combinatory Logic in Array Languages](https://github.com/codereport/Content/blob/main/Publications/Combinatory_Logic_and_Combinators_in_Array_Languages.pdf) I discovered that S' was really Φ and and the missing E^ like combinator was Φ₁. I introduced the named "Pheasant" to match the Smullyan naming convention (so it is now Φ = Phoenix and Φ₁ = Pheasant).

This is follow up to https://github.com/mlochbaum/BQN/pull/53

Signed-off-by: leecalcote <leecalcote@gmail.com>

**Description**

This PR fixes #3008.

I tried the number of configuration combinations for the [gatsby-plugin-sitemap](https://www.gatsbyjs.com/plugins/gatsby-plugin-sitemap/) plug-in, but couldn't find any of which that would land the sitemap.xml in the root directory. 

Two solutions to getting the sitemap.xml back to the route directories or 1) creating a redirect or 2) downgrading to v3.x of the plug-in. 

For now, we're moving to /sitemap/sitemap-index.xml as an index of sitemap files. I've updated Google Search Console and the robots.txt file to point to this new location. It might not hurt to have a redirect from `/sitemap.xml` to this new location...

body:
- Add an explicit flag for post-build signing
- In-build signing is only supported on Windows. This repo creates some packages on Mac and Linux, and at the moment they can only be created on those platforms. When post build signing isn't enabled, download the artifacts for those platforms and run the sign and publish phases of the build.
- Update the cert for the MSIs to be the .NET Cert
- Move the PostBuildSIgn flag into the YAML so it can be used in template expressions
- Pass -sign (harmless if post-build sign is on) in all ci cases.
- Always publish even on PRs, there's no harm in it.

author: davidzech27
body:
I fixed a few bugs that I noticed.
### Fix making arguments lowercase
When parsing the arguments, the program calls the "lower" function on them to make them case-insensitive. The file paths of inputted Dicom folders will be modified, and won't be found later if they use capital letters in them since file paths are case-sensitive. I changed the code to only use the lower function on the argument switch variable, not the actual argument itself.
### Fix appending directory separator to Dicom folder argument
When appending a trailing directory separator character to inputted Dicom folders, it assumes that the program is being run on Window. It appends a "\\" character instead of a "/". I added some code to check if the program is being run on Windows in order to append the correct character.
### Fix issue with xmlParams
When saving xmlParams in proceedCallback, the program indexes aValues using parentheses instead of curly brackets. Because aValues is a cell array, this indexes a subset of aValues instead of a single element in it. So, xmlParams will be populated with 1x1 cell arrays instead of the values in them. I changed the parentheses to curly brackets to fix this.
### Fix type of values from checkboxes
When creating a checkbox, the program initializes the field's aValue as the value gotten from the xml file, but doesn't convert it from type string to double. What I noticed before changing this was that before the checkbox was checked or unchecked by the user, its aValue would be a string, and after it was changed, it would be a double. I added in a type conversion to fix this.
### Fix updating checkbox values
When updating aValues in uiCallback, the program sets the new value for checkboxes to hObject.String, even though the value of the checkbox is actually stored in its "Value" property. I changed "hObject.String" to "hObject.Value".

author: piercetrey-figure
body:
* if bootstrapping with the batch size set to 1 (or anything less than a contract's number of records + 1) could lead to a bad bootstrap if the process is interrupted between when the contract spec is created on chain and when the record specifications were created, as a subsequent run of the same code would produce the same hash, resulting in the record spec creation being skipped and subsequent operations using a session of that contract spec could fail due to missing record specs
* The bootstrapping process is now smarter and checks for contract spec existence, creates it if it doesn't exist, but also checks for record spec existence and will create any non-existent record specs even if the parent contract spec does exist
